header.title: How to Fix a Broken Coaxial Cable
header.description: This guide explains how to repair a damaged coaxial cable by removing the broken section and using electrical tape and connectors to create a secure, functional connection.

steps.description: Repair minor cable damage by applying liquid electrical tape or replacing the cable end.
actions: If insulation is damaged but the line is intact, use a paintbrush to carefully spread liquid electrical tape over the damaged area.
Ensure the damaged area is sufficiently covered with liquid electrical tape.
Allow the liquid electrical tape ample time to dry.
If the cable end is damaged, disconnect the cable.
Twist off the damaged cable end.
Replace the end with a new end.
Twist the new end onto the cable in a counterclockwise fashion.

steps.description: Cut out the damaged area of the cable using cable cutters after ensuring the cable is disconnected.
actions: Ensure the cable is safely disconnected

steps.description: This step involves connecting replacement ends to the shortened wires of the cable after removing the damaged portion.
actions: Strip back half of the cable's black outer insulation.
Fold the cable's silver-braided wire over the outer insulation.
Strip back half of the cable's inner insulation and expose the copper wiring.
Twist the replacement ends on in a counterclockwise fashion.
Join the ends together with the coax cable joiner.
Apply a new protective layer of insulation with a paintbrush and liquid electrical tape.
Allow the liquid tape ample time to dry.
